documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation Note
documents.content:
## Patient: Robert, 35yo cis female

**HPI:** Acute cholecystitis presenting with symptomatic cholelithiasis. Reports of abdominal pain localized to the right upper quadrant, radiating to the right flank.  Patient denies fever or chills.

**Physical Exam:** Vital signs within normal limits. Abdomen soft and non-tender to palpation. Bowel sounds present and regular. Murphy’s sign positive. No rebound tenderness.

**Management Plan:** Laparoscopic cholecystectomy performed successfully, achieving complete gallbladder resection with no operative distress.  Antibiotics initiated postoperatively as per protocol. Patient educated on dietary modifications and potential complications. Discharge home with pain management and follow-up appointment in 3 days.

diagnostics.conclusion: Right Upper Quadrant Abdominal Ultrasound abnormal findings: Acute Cholecystitis with symptomatic cholelithiasis. Key indicators: gallbladder wall thickening, cholelithiasis.
